questions.question: Find the product of the common prime factors of the numbers 1950, 1560 and 2340.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the **HCF** of the given numbers: **1950**, **1560**, and **2340**.

Divide by common divisor 10: 195, 156, 234.

Divide by common divisor 13: 15, 12, 18.

Divide by common divisor 3: 5, 4, 6.

Product of common divisors = 10 × 13 × 3 = **390**.

Prime factors of 390 are 2, 3, 5, and 13. Their product is 390.

**∴ The correct answer is 390.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers are **1950**, **1560**, and **2340**.

**Formula Used:** Prime factorization method to find common factors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9e1f50741b94ee2250c0419b33c8eeee74410f9aa089cff33a26ef576e593a2c.png] 

Perform prime factorization for each number:

⇒ 1950 = 2¹ × 3¹ × 5² × 13¹

⇒ 1560 = 2³ × 3¹ × 5¹ × 13¹

⇒ 2340 = 2² × 3² × 5¹ × 13¹

Identify the **common prime factors** present in all three numbers:

⇒ The common primes are **2, 3, 5, and 13**.

Calculate the **product** of these common prime factors:

⇒ Product = 2 × 3 × 5 × 13

⇒ Product = 6 × 65 = 390

**∴ The correct answer is 390.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The **HCF** is the product of the lowest powers of all common prime factors. In this case, HCF = 2¹ × 3¹ × 5¹ × 13¹ = 390.

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The **LCM** is the product of the highest powers of all prime factors involved in the numbers. For these numbers, LCM = 2³ × 3² × 5² × 13¹ = 23400.

Prime Factorization

Every composite number can be expressed as a unique product of **prime numbers**. Common prime factors are those primes that appear in the factorization of all given numbers.

questions.question: During a sale 50% of the goods are sold at 40% profit, 40% of the remaining goods are sold at 13% profit and the still remaining goods are sold at a loss of 32%. If there is an overall profit of x%, then what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Weighted average profit % = (Portion₁ × P₁ + Portion₂ × P₂ + Portion₃ × P₃)

Portion 1 = 50%; Portion 2 = 40% of 50% = 20%; Portion 3 = 100% − 50% − 20% = 30%

Net profit x = (0.50 × 40) + (0.20 × 13) + (0.30 × −32)

x = 20 + 2.6 − 9.6 = 13

**∴ The correct answer is 13.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total goods = 100 units (Assumed CP = ₹1/unit, Total CP = ₹100)

First part = 50% of 100 = 50 units at 40% **profit**.

Second part = 40% of **remaining goods** (50) = 20 units at 13% **profit**.

Third part = still **remaining goods** = 100 − 50 − 20 = 30 units at 32% **loss**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e58dd4ec31bd5580daa042ee7e28a9bafeb0aad5935de65d0e6c3a850b3e0f1a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Profit from Part 1 = 40% of 50 = (40 ÷ 100) × 50 = ₹20

⇒ Profit from Part 2 = 13% of 20 = (13 ÷ 100) × 20 = ₹2.6

⇒ Loss from Part 3 = 32% of 30 = (32 ÷ 100) × 30 = ₹9.6

⇒ Total Net Profit = 20 + 2.6 − 9.6 = ₹13

⇒ **Overall profit x%** = (Total Profit ÷ Total CP) × 100

⇒ x = (13 ÷ 100) × 100 = 13

**∴ The correct answer is 13.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Profit Formula

When items are sold in different parts, the net profit/loss percentage is given by (n₁p₁ + n₂p₂ + ...) ÷ (n₁ + n₂ + ...), where n is quantity and p is profit%.

Successive Percentage of Remainder

If a% is removed, and then b% of the remaining is taken, the second part as a percentage of the whole is b × (100 − a) ÷ 100.

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit % = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100. A loss is treated as a negative profit in calculation of the overall net change.

questions.question: If x is the third proportional to 2 and y, and y is the third proportional to x and 18, then what is the value of y?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If **c** is the **third proportional** to **a** and **b**, then **c = b²/a**.

Given **x = y²/2** and **y = 18²/x**.

Substituting **x**: y = 324 ÷ (y²/2) ⇒ y = 648/y².

y³ = 648 ⇒ y = ³√(216 × 3) = 6³√3.

**∴ The correct answer is 6³√3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First set: 2, **y**, and **x** are in **continued proportion**.

Second set: **x**, 18, and **y** are in **continued proportion**.

**Formula Used:**

If **a : b = b : c**, then **b² = ac**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ff5bdb71a42b86a662baea06fa2e10912f237be2151cc4d1eadfe646fdd938c0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ From the first condition: y² = 2 × x ⇒ **x = y²/2**

⇒ From the second condition: 18² = x × y ⇒ **324 = xy**

⇒ Substituting the value of **x** in the second equation:

⇒ 324 = (y²/2) × y

⇒ 324 × 2 = y³

⇒ y³ = 648

⇒ y = ³√(216 × 3)

⇒ y = 6 × ³√3

**∴ The correct answer is 6³√3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers **a** and **b** is defined as **√(ab)**.

Fourth Proportional

If **a : b :: c : d**, then **d** is the fourth proportional to **a, b, c** and is calculated as **d = (b × c) / a**.

Third Proportional

If **a : b :: b : c**, then **c** is the third proportional to **a** and **b**, calculated as **c = b² / a**.

Continued Proportion

Three numbers **a, b, c** are in continued proportion if the ratio of the first to the second is equal to the ratio of the second to the third (**a/b = b/c**).

questions.question:
If the surface area of a sphere is 314 cm², find its radius.

(Take π = 3.14)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Directly apply the relation: 4r² = **Surface Area** ÷ π

4r² = 314 ÷ 3.14 = 100

r² = 100 ÷ 4 = 25

r = √25 = 5 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Surface Area (SA)** of the **sphere** = 314 cm²

Value of π = 3.14

**Formula Used:**

**Surface Area** of a **sphere** = 4 × π × r²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0852459b32feaa71fcb37ac63d5ed124cc26731032c764c9cf11554dea4d6844.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 314 = 4 × 3.14 × r²

⇒ 314 = 12.56 × r²

⇒ r² = 314 ÷ 12.56

⇒ r² = 25

⇒ r = √25

⇒ r = 5 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Sphere

The total space occupied by a sphere is given by Volume = (4/3) × π × r³.

Hemisphere Formulas

For a **hemisphere**: Curved Surface Area = 2πr² and Total Surface Area = 3πr².

Volume of a Hemisphere

The **volume** of a hemisphere is exactly half of a sphere: Volume = (2/3) × π × r³.

questions.question: A, B, C, and D can do a piece of work in 12, 15, 20, and 30 days, respectively. All start together, but D leaves after 2 days, C leaves 3 days before the completion, and B leaves 2 days before the completion. Determine the total time required to complete the work.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Total Work** = LCM(12, 15, 20, 30) = 60 units. Efficiencies: **A=5**, **B=4**, **C=3**, **D=2**.

Subtract work of person leaving **after** starting: 60 − (D × 2) = 60 − 4 = 56 units (D is removed).

Add work of persons leaving **before** completion: 56 + (C × 3) + (B × 2) = 56 + 9 + 8 = 73 units.

Total time = Adjusted Work ÷ (Sum of efficiencies of A, B, and C) = 73 ÷ 12 = 6¹/₁₂ days.

Converting fraction to hours: ¹/₁₂ × 24 = 2 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 days 2 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by **A** = 12 days, **B** = 15 days, **C** = 20 days, and **D** = 30 days.

⇒ **D** works for 2 days, **C** works for (x − 3) days, **B** works for (x − 2) days, and **A** works for all x days.

⇒ Total work equation: (5 × x) + 4 × (x − 2) + 3 × (x − 3) + (2 × 2) = 60

Leaving Before vs. After Completion

If a person leaves **n days after starting**, subtract their work and exclude them. If they leave **n days before completion**, add their hypothetical work and keep them in the divisor.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the **actual work done** by each person, which is (Efficiency × Time Spent).

Pipes and Cisterns Analogy

questions.question: When one-third of a number is increased by 87, the result is 107. Find the sum of the digits of the original number.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Value of **one-third** of the number = 107 − 87 = 20.

Original Number = 20 × 3 = 60.

Sum of digits of the number = 6 + 0 = 6.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Result after increasing one-third of a number by 87 = 107

**Formula Used:**

Linear Equation: (1/n) × x + c = R (where x is the original number)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ede7001dc6ef27e04b42ac171a04c412566c89bfd03f121d7723d805aae34173.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the **original number** be x.

⇒ (1/3) × x + 87 = 107

⇒ x/3 = 107 − 87

⇒ x/3 = 20

⇒ x = 20 × 3

⇒ x = 60

Now, calculate the **sum of the digits** of the number 60:

⇒ Sum = 6 + 0 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations

A linear equation in one variable is an equation which can be written in the form ax + b = 0, where a and b are constants and x is the variable.

Sum of Digits Property

The sum of the digits is often used in **divisibility rules**. For example, a number is divisible by 3 or 9 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3 or 9 respectively.

Fraction Manipulation

To find the whole from a part, multiply the value of the part by the **reciprocal** of the fraction (e.g., if 1/n = V, then Total = V × n).

questions.question: If a sum of ₹8000 becomes thrice of itself after 8 years on compound interest, then how much will it become after 24 years?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **Compound Interest**, if a sum becomes **n times** in **t years**, it becomes **nk times** in **k × t years**.

Given: Sum becomes **3 times** in **8 years**.

Target time = **24 years** ⇒ **k = 24 ÷ 8 = 3**.

New Amount = **Principal × 3³** ⇒ **8000 × 27** = **₹216000**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹216000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹8000

**Time (t)** = 8 years, **Amount (A)** = 3P

**Total Time (T)** = 24 years

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/749bea53b27870f6d3e293d2506e8a46e39ff547f4400631370465e2aca71e21.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 3P = P(1 + r/100)⁸

⇒ (1 + r/100)⁸ = 3

⇒ For 24 years, Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)²⁴

⇒ A = 8000 × [(1 + r/100)⁸]³

⇒ A = 8000 × 3³

⇒ A = 8000 × 27

⇒ A = ₹216000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹216000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

CI Multiplication Property

If a sum grows by a factor of **m** in **t** years, it will grow by a factor of **mk** in **k × t** years.

Rule of 72

To estimate the time required to double an investment, divide **72** by the annual interest rate **r** (Time ≈ 72 ÷ r).

Difference between CI and SI for 2 Years

The difference **D** between CI and SI for 2 years is given by **D = P × (r/100)²**.

questions.question: A can finish a work in 5 days and B can do the same work in 50 days. B worked alone for 10 days and left the job. In how many days can A alone finish the remaining work?

Work done by **B** in **10 days** = 10 × 1 = 10 units.

questions.question: If 15 workers can build a wall in 10 days, how many workers are needed to build it in 6 days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work remains constant: **M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂**

Product of workers and days in first case = Product in second case.

15 × 10 = **M₂** × 6

150 = 6 × **M₂** ⇒ **M₂** = 25

**∴ The correct answer is 25 workers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f5b3c2a12bea10e8eae4b12ac88af435e98f8d5b13b3c2aadb3db7a25206402d.png] 

**Given:**

Initial workers (**M₁**) = 15

Initial days (**D₁**) = 10

Required days (**D₂**) = 6

**Formula Used:**

**M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂**

**Calculations:**

⇒ 15 × 10 = **M₂** × 6

⇒ 150 = 6 × **M₂**

⇒ **M₂** = 150 ÷ 6

⇒ **M₂** = 25

**∴ The correct answer is 25 workers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Chain Rule Formula

The general formula for work problems is (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂, where H is hours and W is work.

Inverse Proportion

For a fixed amount of work, the number of **workers** is inversely proportional to the **time** taken. If time decreases, workers must increase.

Work and Efficiency

Total Work = Total Efficiency × Time. If efficiency of each worker is 1, then Total Work = Number of Workers × Time.

questions.question: Simplify (5z-12y)² + (12z+5y)² - 144z².
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **standard algebraic identity**: (az − by)² + (bz + ay)² = (a² + b²)(z² + y²).

Substitute a = 5 and b = 12: (5² + 12²)(z² + y²) = (25 + 144)(z² + y²) = 169z² + 169y².

Subtract the remaining term: 169z² + 169y² − 144z² = 25z² + 169y².

**∴ The correct answer is 25z² + 169y².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** (5z − 12y)² + (12z + 5y)² − 144z²

**Formulas Used:** (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab and (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

⇒ [(5z)² + (12y)² − 2(5z)(12y)] + [(12z)² + (5y)² + 2(12z)(5y)] − 144z²

⇒ [25z² + 144y² − 120zy] + [144z² + 25y² + 120zy] − 144z²

⇒ 25z² + 144z² − 144z² + 144y² + 25y² − 120zy + 120zy

⇒ 25z² + 169y² + 0

⇒ 25z² + 169y²

**∴ The correct answer is 25z² + 169y².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identities

The square of a **binomial sum** is (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b², while the square of a **binomial difference** is (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b².

Brahmagupta-Fibonacci Identity

The product of two **sums of squares** is itself a sum of squares: (a² + b²)(c² + d²) = (ac − bd)² + (ad + bc)².

Pythagorean Triplet

In this problem, the coefficients 5, 12, and 13 form a **Pythagorean triplet** where 5² + 12² = 13² = 169.

questions.question: A classroom has 46 boys and 36 girls. If the number of girls is increased successively by 25% followed by another 20%, by how many will the number of girls exceed the number of boys?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net percentage increase = x + y + (xy/100)

Successive increase of 25% and 20% = 25 + 20 + (25 × 20 / 100) = 50%

New number of **girls** = 36 + 50% of 36 = 36 + 18 = 54

Difference = 54 − 46 = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

questions.question: The value of 4 + tan²θ + cot²θ - sec²θ cosec²θ is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Substitute a standard angle **θ = 45°** to quickly evaluate the expression.

At θ = 45°: **tan 45° = 1**, **cot 45° = 1**, **sec 45° = √2**, and **cosec 45° = √2**.

Expression = 4 + (1)2 + (1)2 − (√2)2 x (√2)2

Expression = 4 + 1 + 1 − 2 x 2 = 6 − 4 = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The trigonometric expression is 2 + tan²θ + cot²θ − sec²θ cosec²θ.

**Formula Used:**

1. 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ ⇒ tan²θ = sec²θ − 1

2. 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ ⇒ cot²θ = cosec²θ − 1

3. sec²θ + cosec²θ = sec²θ × cosec²θ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aba158eb9b300bf0551f18a34cdc43906884aa679f9bc739b3c59c68c1f2562e.png]

⇒ 4 + tan2θ + cot2θ − sec2θ cosec2θ

⇒ 4 + (sec2θ − 1) + (cosec2θ − 1) − sec2θ cosec2θ

⇒ 4 + sec2θ + cosec2θ − 2 − sec2θ cosec2θ

⇒ 2 + sec2θ + cosec2θ − sec2θ cosec2θ

⇒ 2 + (1/cos2θ + 1/sin2θ) − sec2θ cosec2θ

⇒ 2 + [(sin2θ + cos2θ) / (sin2θ cos2θ)] − sec2θ cosec2θ

⇒ 2 + [1 / (sin2θ cos2θ)] − sec2θ cosec2θ

⇒ 2 + sec2θ cosec2θ − sec2θ cosec2θ = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

Sum-to-Product Identity

For secant and cosecant, the sum of their squares is equal to the product of their squares: sec²θ + cosec²θ = sec²θ × cosec²θ.

Tangent and Cotangent Relation

The expression tan θ + cot θ can be simplified as 1/(sin θ cos θ), which is also equal to sec θ cosec θ.

Pythagorean Identities

Always remember **sin²θ + cos²θ = 1**, **1 + tan²θ = sec²θ**, and **1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ** as they are the building blocks for such simplifications.

questions.question: Two trains of lengths 120 m and 180 m are running in opposite directions at speeds of 60 km/h and 75 km/h, respectively. In how many seconds will they completely cross each other?

**Relative Speed** in **opposite directions** = 60 + 75 = 135 km/h.

Convert to m/s: 135 × 5/18 = 37.5 m/s.

**Total Distance** = Sum of lengths = 120 + 180 = 300 m.

Time = 300 ÷ 37.5 = 8 sec.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Length of Train 2 (L₂) = **180 m**

Speed of Train 1 (S₁) = **60 km/h**

Speed of Train 2 (S₂) = **75 km/h**

**Formula Used:**

Time = (Total Distance) ÷ (Relative Speed)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c1330430a3da296cfad8e9d5bfc387381d10695dec4a1949be64096ecdd4640b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 120 + 180 = **300 m**

⇒ Relative Speed (Opposite Directions) = S₁ + S₂

⇒ Relative Speed = 60 + 75 = **135 km/h**

⇒ Convert speed to m/s = 135 × (5 ÷ 18)

⇒ Relative Speed = 7.5 × 5 = **37.5 m/s**

⇒ Time taken = 300 ÷ 37.5

⇒ Time taken = 3000 ÷ 375 = **8 sec**

**∴ The correct answer is 8 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in **opposite directions**, relative speed is S₁ + S₂. When they move in the **same direction**, relative speed is |S₁ − S₂|.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert from **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing Stationary Objects

Time to cross a **pole or man** = Train Length ÷ Speed. Time to cross a **platform or bridge** = (Train Length + Platform Length) ÷ Speed.

Arithmetic Mean (Average)

questions.question: If a number is added to each of the numbers 16, 20 and 30, then the resulting numbers are in the continued proportion. Find the mean proportional between the largest and smallest of the resulting numbers.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For numbers **a, b, c** to be in **continued proportion** by adding **x**, use the shortcut: **x = (b² − ac) / (a + c − 2b)**.

Here, a = 16, b = 20, c = 30 ⇒ x = (20² − 16 × 30) / (16 + 30 − 2 × 20) = (400 − 480) / (46 − 40) = −80 / 6 = −40/3.

**Smallest number** = 16 − 40/3 = 8/3 | **Largest number** = 30 − 40/3 = 50/3.

**Mean proportional** = √(Smallest × Largest) = √(8/3 × 50/3) = √(400/9) = 20/3.

**∴ The correct answer is 20/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial numbers are **16, 20, 30**. A number **x** is added to each.

**Formula Used:** If a, b, c are in **continued proportion**, then **b² = ac**. The **mean proportional** of m and n is **√(m × n)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4106555701c21f2033cb3431946e8a7cb8deb94cf285511709367b0756725b5a.png] 

⇒ Resulting numbers: **(16 + x), (20 + x), (30 + x)**

⇒ According to the condition: (16 + x) / (20 + x) = (20 + x) / (30 + x)

⇒ (16 + x)(30 + x) = (20 + x)²

⇒ 480 + 16x + 30x + x² = 400 + 40x + x²

⇒ 480 + 46x = 400 + 40x

⇒ 46x − 40x = 400 − 480

⇒ 6x = −80 ⇒ **x = −40/3**

⇒ Smallest number = 16 − 40/3 = (48 − 40) / 3 = **8/3**

⇒ Largest number = 30 − 40/3 = (90 − 40) / 3 = **50/3**

⇒ Mean proportional = √(8/3 × 50/3) = √(400/9) = **20/3**

**∴ The correct answer is 20/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The **mean proportional** between two numbers **a** and **b** is defined as **x = √(ab)**, such that a : x = x : b.

Third Proportional

If three numbers **a, b, and c** are in **continued proportion** (a/b = b/c), then **c** is called the **third proportional** and **c = b²/a**.

Fourth Proportional

If four numbers **a, b, c, and d** are in proportion (a : b = c : d), then **d** is the **fourth proportional** and **d = (b × c) / a**.

questions.question: A person borrows ₹10,000 for 3 years at 5% per annum simple interest. He immediately lends it to another person at 8(1)/(4)\% per annum simple interest for 3 years. What is his gain (in ₹) in the transaction per year?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Gain per year** is the difference between the lending rate and the borrowing rate applied to the **Principal**.

Rate difference = 8(1/4)% − 5% = 8.25% − 5% = 3.25%

Gain per year = 3.25% of ₹10,000

Gain per year = (3.25 ÷ 100) × 10,000 = 3.25 × 100 = ₹325

**∴ The correct answer is ₹325.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Borrowing Rate (R₁)** = 5% per annum

**Lending Rate (R₂)** = 8(1/4)% = 8.25% per annum

**Time (T)** = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1ecb0ef9306c9680975704314887d02ed09a47a1ce7cbde99b7c576e3f14cd6f.png]

⇒ Total Gain in 3 years = Interest earned − Interest paid

⇒ Total Gain = 2,475 − 1,500 = ₹975

⇒ Gain in the transaction **per year** = 975 ÷ 3

⇒ Gain per year = ₹325

**∴ The correct answer is ₹325.**

Simple Interest Principle

Simple interest is calculated only on the initial principal amount of a loan or deposit. Formula: SI = P × R × T ÷ 100.

Effective Gain Rate

Compound Interest vs Simple Interest

Unlike SI, Compound Interest is calculated on the principal plus any accumulated interest from previous periods. Amount = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ.

questions.question: The value of a machine is first depreciated by 20%. It is then appreciated by 25% and finally depreciated by 10%. Find the overall percentage change in its value.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Successive Multiplying Factor** method.

Net Multiplying Factor = 0.80 (20% decrease) × 1.25 (25% increase) × 0.90 (10% decrease)

Net Factor = (0.80 × 1.25) × 0.90 = 1.00 × 0.90 = 0.90

Overall Change % = (Final Factor − 1) × 100 = (0.90 − 1) × 100 = −10%

A negative sign indicates a **percentage decrease**.

**∴ The correct answer is 10% decrease.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First Change = 20% **Depreciation** (−)

Second Change = 25% **Appreciation** (+)

Third Change = 10% **Depreciation** (−)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5be4600d6f7a5a892a31175da9f82cb6e7e5b142bf7503382f07af26b676f4dc.png] 

Let the **Initial Value** of the machine be 100.

⇒ Value after 20% depreciation = 100 − (20% of 100) = 100 − 20 = 80

⇒ Value after 25% appreciation = 80 + (25% of 80) = 80 + 20 = 100

⇒ Value after 10% depreciation = 100 − (10% of 100) = 100 − 10 = 90

⇒ Total change in value = 100 − 90 = 10

⇒ Overall Percentage Change = (Total Change ÷ Initial Value) × 100

⇒ Overall Percentage Change = (10 ÷ 100) × 100 = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10% decrease.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change Formula

For two successive percentage changes of a% and b%, the effective change is given by the formula: [a + b + (ab/100)]%.

Fractional Equivalents

Calculations become faster using fractions: 20% = 1/5, 25% = 1/4, and 10% = 1/10. For depreciation, multiply by (1 − fraction), and for appreciation, multiply by (1 + fraction).

Net Change Principle

The order of percentage changes does not affect the final result. A 20% decrease followed by a 25% increase results in the same final value as a 25% increase followed by a 20% decrease.

Empirical Relationship Constraints

Symmetrical Distribution

questions.question: The length of one of the two parallel sides of a trapezium is 8 cm, while the length of the other side of this pair of parallel sides is equal to the distance between this pair of parallel sides. If the area of the trapezium is 120 cm², then what is the distance (in cm) between the said pair of parallel sides?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of **trapezium** = ½ × (Sum of parallel sides) × **Height**

Given: Side 1 = 8 cm, Side 2 = h, Height = h, Area = 120 cm²

⇒ 120 = ½ × (8 + h) × h ⇒ h(h + 8) = 240

By checking options: If **h = 12**, then 12 × (12 + 8) = 12 × 20 = 240 (Matches!)

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/762c9d73882723ff5ba6b6142827632572cff92704c84a0a3b52b0bf96f602bd.png] 

**Given:**

⇒ **Parallel side a** = 8 cm

⇒ **Parallel side b** = **Distance h**

⇒ **Area** = 120 cm²

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Area of Trapezium = ½ × (a + b) × h

**Calculations:**

⇒ 120 = ½ × (8 + h) × h

⇒ 240 = 8h + h²

⇒ h² + 8h − 240 = 0

⇒ h² + 20h − 12h − 240 = 0

⇒ h(h + 20) − 12(h + 20) = 0

⇒ (h − 12)(h + 20) = 0

⇒ Since h cannot be negative, **h = 12 cm**.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Trapezium

It is defined as the product of the average of the parallel sides and the vertical distance between them: Area = ½ × (sum of parallel sides) × h.

Median of a Trapezium

questions.question: In a row of 29 people facing north, Karan is 9th from the right end. If Ramesh sits fifth to the left of Karan, what is Ramesh’s position from the left end of the line?

Total number of people in the row = **29**

Position of **Karan** from the **right end** = 9th

Position from the **left end** = (Total number of people − Position from the right end) + 1

= (29 − 14) + 1

= 15 + 1

= 16th

So, **Ramesh** is 16th from the **left end**.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1"**.

__
 
• The calculation is based on the **Law of Definite Proportions** (also known as **Proust's Law**), which states that a chemical compound always contains its component elements in a **fixed ratio** by mass, regardless of its source.
 
• Given that **9 g of water** contains **1 g of hydrogen** and **8 g of oxygen**, the mass ratio of Hydrogen to Oxygen in water is established as **1:8**.
 
• To determine the components in **36 g of water**, we calculate the proportionality constant by dividing the target mass by the reference mass: 36 g ÷ 9 g = **4**.
 
• By applying this factor of **4** to the original components, the mass of hydrogen required is 1 g × 4 = **4 g**.
 
• Similarly, the mass of oxygen required is 8 g × 4 = **32 g**.
 
• The sum of the individual masses (4 g + 32 g) equals the total mass of **36 g**, satisfying the **Law of Conservation of Mass**.

questions.question: The process wherein the body of the living organism splits into two exactly identical halves is termed as ___________.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Binary fission** is a specific type of **asexual reproduction** where a single parent organism divides into **two equal and identical** daughter cells.
 
• The process initiates with the **replication of DNA**, ensuring each new cell receives a copy of the genetic blueprint.
 
• This is followed by **karyokinesis**, the division of the nucleus, and subsequent **cytokinesis**, the division of the cytoplasm and organelles.
 
• It is the most common mode of reproduction in **prokaryotic organisms** such as **Bacteria** and **Archaea**, allowing for exponential population growth in **favorable environments**.
 
• In **unicellular eukaryotes** like **Amoeba**, the division can happen in any plane, whereas in **Leishmania**, which has a flagellum at one end, division occurs in a **longitudinal plane**.
 
• Because the daughter cells are genetically identical to the parent, they are considered **clones**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Budding**:

 
 
• A process where a new individual develops as an outgrowth or **bud** from the parent body due to **repeated cell division** at a specific site.
 
• Commonly observed in organisms like **Yeast** (unicellular) and **Hydra** (multicellular).
 
 
 
• **Multiple Fission**:
 
 
• A method where a single parent cell divides into **many daughter cells** simultaneously.
 
• The malarial parasite **Plasmodium** uses this method to replicate rapidly within a host cell.
 
 
 
• **Fragmentation**:
 
 
• Occurs when a multicellular organism breaks into **multiple pieces** or fragments upon reaching maturity, and each piece regenerates into a new organism.
 
• This is a characteristic reproductive method for **Spirogyra** and certain **planarians**.

options.text: Photosynthesis is restricted to night-time only to minimise water loss.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Desert plants, categorized as **Xerophytes**, utilize a specialized photosynthetic adaptation known as **Crassulacean Acid Metabolism (CAM)** to survive in extremely arid conditions.
 
• To prevent excessive water loss through **Transpiration**, these plants keep their **Stomata** tightly closed during the day when temperatures are high.
 
• At night, the **Stomata** open to take in **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)** from the atmosphere, which is then fixed into **Malic Acid** and stored in the cell **Vacuoles**.
 
• During the following day, the stored **Malic Acid** is transported out of the vacuole and broken down to release **Carbon Dioxide** internally within the leaf cells.
 
• This internal **CO2** is then processed through the **Calvin Cycle** using the energy (**ATP** and **NADPH**) generated by the **Light-Dependent Reactions** occurring in the **Chloroplasts**.
 
• This temporal separation of **Carbon Fixation** and the **Calvin Cycle** ensures the plant can perform photosynthesis while conserving maximum water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Photosynthetic Pathways**:

 
 
• **C3 Plants**: Fix carbon directly into a 3-carbon compound during the day; they are common in temperate regions but lose significant water in heat.
 
• **C4 Plants**: Separate carbon fixation and the Calvin cycle spatially in different cell types (**Mesophyll** and **Bundle Sheath** cells).
 
• **CAM Plants**: Examples include **Cacti**, **Pineapples**, **Agave**, and **Aloe Vera**, which separate these processes by time (Night vs. Day).
 
 
 
• **Ecological Importance**:
 
 
• The **Water-Use Efficiency (WUE)** of CAM plants is significantly higher than that of C3 or C4 plants, allowing them to inhabit regions where **Precipitation** is scarce.
 
• The **Waxy Cuticle** on the surface of these plants further assists in reducing non-stomatal water loss.

questions.question: What will be the wavelength of a sound wave whose frequency is 220 Hz and speed is 440 m/s in a given medium?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The physical relationship between the **velocity** of a wave, its **frequency**, and its **wavelength** is defined by the fundamental wave equation: **v = f × λ**. This principle applies to all periodic waves, including **acoustic** and **electromagnetic** waves.
 
• The **frequency (f)** of the sound wave is given as **220 Hz**. In physics, frequency represents the number of cycles or vibrations that occur in **one second**. The unit **Hertz (Hz)** is equivalent to **s−¹**.
 
• The **speed of sound (v)** in the specific medium is provided as **440 m/s**. The speed of a wave depends on the **density** and **elasticity** of the medium through which it travels.
 
• To solve for the **wavelength (λ)**, the equation is rearranged to **λ = v / f**. Wavelength is the spatial distance between two consecutive corresponding points of the wave, such as two **compressions** or **rarefactions**.
 
• By substituting the given values: **λ = 440 / 220**. Dividing the velocity by the frequency yields a result of **2 m**. This means the wave repeats its pattern every 2 meters in that medium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sound Waves**:

 
 
• Sound is a **mechanical wave** that requires a material medium (solid, liquid, or gas) for propagation. It is characterized as a **longitudinal wave** because the particles of the medium oscillate parallel to the direction of wave motion.
 
• In air at standard room temperature (**20°C**), the speed of sound is approximately **343 m/s**, whereas it is significantly faster in liquids like **water** (approx. **1480 m/s**) and solids like **iron** (approx. **5120 m/s**).
 
 
 
• **Human Audibility**:
 
 
• The standard **audible range** for human beings is between **20 Hz and 20,000 Hz**. The frequency in this problem (**220 Hz**) falls well within this range and corresponds to a relatively low pitch.
 
• Frequencies below 20 Hz are termed **infrasonic**, while those above 20 kHz are termed **ultrasonic**.
 
 
 
• **Wavelength and Energy**:
 
 
• In a given medium, because wave speed is constant for a specific set of conditions, the wavelength is **inversely proportional** to the frequency. Therefore, higher frequency sounds have **shorter wavelengths**.

• While most of the **cartilaginous skeleton** in vertebrate embryos is replaced by **bone** in adults, cartilage remains in critical locations such as the **tip of the nose**, **external ear joints** (pinna), and **intervertebral discs**.
 
• It also forms **articular cartilage** at the **ends of long bones**, where it provides a smooth, lubricated surface to facilitate **low-friction movement** within joints.

• It serves as a **support framework** for the **epithelium** and contains cells like **fibroblasts**, **macrophages**, and **mast cells**.
 
 
 
• **Adipose tissue**:
 
 
• Another type of **loose connective tissue** specialized for the **storage of fats**.
 
• It is found mainly beneath the skin and acts as an **insulator** and energy reservoir.
 
 
 
• **Bone**:
 
 
• A **dense connective tissue** with a **hard** and **non-pliable** ground substance.
 
• It is rich in **calcium salts** and **collagen fibers**, which give bone its strength to provide the primary **structural frame** of the body.

questions.question: Which of the following situations shows zero acceleration?

options.text: A car moving with constant speed on a straight road

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A car moving with constant speed on a straight road**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acceleration** is defined as the **rate of change of velocity** over time. It is represented by the formula **a = (v − u) / t**, where **v** is the final velocity and **u** is the initial velocity.
 
• **Velocity** is a **vector quantity**, meaning it possesses both **magnitude (speed)** and **direction**. Acceleration occurs if either the speed or the direction of motion changes.
 
• In the case of a car moving at a **constant speed** on a **straight road**, the magnitude of velocity is unchanging, and the direction is fixed. Therefore, the change in velocity (**Δv**) is zero, resulting in **zero acceleration**.
 
• According to **Newton's First Law of Motion**, an object moving with **constant velocity** has a net external force of zero acting upon it, which is consistent with the condition of zero acceleration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ball thrown upward**:

 
 
• An object thrown vertically experiences a constant **acceleration due to gravity (g)**, which is approximately **9.8 m/s²** downward.
 
• Even at the peak of its trajectory where instantaneous velocity is zero, the acceleration remains **non-zero**.
 
 
 
• **A train speeding up**:
 
 
• When a vehicle increases its speed, it undergoes **positive acceleration**.
 
• This involves a change in the **magnitude of velocity** over a specific time interval.
 
 
 
• **An aeroplane taking off**:
 
 
• During a takeoff roll, an aircraft accelerates from a standstill to reach its **liftoff speed**.
 
• This represents a significant **linear acceleration** required to generate the necessary **aerodynamic lift**.
 
 
 
• **Uniform Circular Motion**:
 
 
• Even if an object moves at a **constant speed** in a circle, its **direction** changes at every point.
 
• This change in direction results in **centripetal acceleration** directed toward the center of the path.

questions.question: Why is biological magnification a health risk even with limited pesticide use?

options.text: Pesticides affect only soil microorganisms, not higher organisms
Non-biodegradable pesticides accumulate at successive trophic levels
The toxicity of pesticides decreases as they move up the food chain
Non-biodegradable pesticides are immediately excreted and do not persist

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Non-biodegradable pesticides accumulate at successive trophic levels**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Biological magnification**, or biomagnification, is the process where certain **toxic substances**, such as **pesticides** or **heavy metals**, increase in concentration as they move up the **food chain**.
 
• These chemicals are **non-biodegradable**, meaning they cannot be broken down by **biological processes** or enzymes within an organism's body.
 
• Because these substances are often **fat-soluble**, they are not excreted through urine but are instead stored in the **adipose tissues** of organisms at each **trophic level**.
 
• As a predator eats multiple prey items, it ingests all the accumulated toxins from those individuals, leading to a exponentially higher concentration in the **top consumers**.
 
• Since **humans** occupy the highest **trophic level** in many ecological systems, the maximum concentration of these harmful chemicals gets accumulated in our bodies, leading to **chronic health issues**, **reproductive failure**, and **hormonal imbalances**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Common Biomagnifiers**:

 
 
• **DDT (Dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane)**: A classic example of a pesticide that caused bird eggshells to thin, leading to population declines in **bald eagles**.
 
• **Mercury**: Often found in **aquatic ecosystems**, it magnifies in fish like **tuna** and **swordfish**, posing risks to human neurological health.
 
 
 
• **Bioaccumulation vs. Biomagnification**:
 
 
• **Bioaccumulation** refers to the build-up of a substance within a **single organism** over its lifetime.
 
• **Biomagnification** refers to the increase in concentration as the substance transfers from **one trophic level to the next**.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Ecosystems**:
 
 
• The accumulation of toxins can disrupt the **energy flow** and **nutrient cycling** by killing off key species or reducing their **reproductive success**.

questions.question: Which calculation correctly determines the formula unit mass of CaCl₂?

options.text: Atomic mass of Ca + (atomic mass of Cl ÷ 2) = 40 + 17.75 = 57.75 u
Atomic mass of Ca + atomic mass of Cl = 40 + 35.5 = 75.5 u
Atomic mass of Ca × atomic mass of Cl = 40 × 35.5 = 1420 u
Atomic mass of Ca + (2 × atomic mass of Cl) = 40 + 71 = 111 u

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atomic mass of Ca + (2 times atomic mass of Cl) = 40 + 71 = 111 u**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **formula unit mass** of a substance is defined as the sum of the **atomic masses** of all atoms present in the formula unit of an ionic compound. It is numerically equivalent to **molecular mass** but used specifically for compounds composed of **ions**.
 
• In the chemical formula for **Calcium Chloride (CaCl₂)**, there is one atom of **Calcium (Ca)** and two atoms of **Chlorine (Cl)**.
 
• The **atomic mass of Calcium (Ca)** is approximately **40 u**. Calcium is a group 2 **alkaline earth metal** with an atomic number of 20.
 
• The **atomic mass of Chlorine (Cl)** is approximately **35.5 u**. This fractional value is the weighted average of its naturally occurring isotopes, **Chlorine-35** and **Chlorine-37**.
 
• To calculate the **formula unit mass**, the mass of **Ca** is added to twice the mass of **Cl**: **40 + (2 × 35.5)**.
 
• Multiplying the mass of **Chlorine** by two gives **71 u**. Adding this to the **40 u** of **Calcium** results in a total of **111 u**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Calcium (Ca)**:

 
 
• It is an essential **alkaline earth metal** used in construction, cement production, and biological functions like bone mineralization.
 
• In **CaCl₂**, it exists as a **Ca²⁺** cation.
 
 
 
• **Chlorine (Cl)**:
 
 
• It is a highly reactive **halogen** found in **Group 17** of the periodic table.
 
• In **CaCl₂**, it exists as two **Cl−** anions to balance the charge of the calcium ion.
 
 
 
• **Unified Atomic Mass Unit (u)**:
 
 
• The unit **u** represents the **unified atomic mass unit**, where 1 u is exactly **1/12th** the mass of an atom of **Carbon-12**.
 
• It is approximately equal to **1.66 × 10−²⁷ kg**.
 
 
 
• **Stoichiometry and Bonding**:
 
 
• **Calcium Chloride** is an **ionic compound** formed by the **electrostatic attraction** between oppositely charged ions.
 
• The formula **CaCl₂** represents the simplest whole-number ratio of ions in the **crystal lattice**.

questions.question: What is the work done on an object if its displacement is zero, even when a force is applied?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zero**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the field of physics, **work done** is defined as the product of the component of the **force** acting on an object and the **displacement** caused by that force in its own direction.
 
• The mathematical expression for work is **W = F × s × cos(θ)**, where **W** represents work, **F** denotes the magnitude of the applied force, **s** is the magnitude of the displacement, and **θ** is the angle between the force and displacement vectors.
 
• When an object remains stationary (**s = 0**) despite the application of an external force, the total **mechanical work** performed on the object is calculated as **W = F × 0 × cos(θ) = 0**.
 
• This scenario occurs frequently in real-world situations, such as a person pushing against a **load-bearing wall** or a student holding a heavy **textbook** at a constant height; although biological energy is consumed, no **physical work** is done on the objects because they do not move.
 
• Since work measures the **transfer of energy**, a lack of displacement implies that no energy has been transferred to the object to change its **kinetic** or **potential energy** state through that specific force.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Variations of Work Done**:

 
 
• **Positive Work**: Occurs when the force and displacement are in the **same direction** (0° ≤ θ 
 
 
• **Standard Units**:
 
 
• The **SI unit** of work is the **Joule (J)**, named after the English physicist **James Prescott Joule**.
 
• One Joule is defined as the work done by a force of one **Newton** causing a displacement of one **meter**.

questions.question: The resistivity of an alloy is generally higher than its constituent metals, and this property makes alloys suitable for ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Heating elements (e.g., nichrome)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **alloy** is a metallic substance composed of two or more elements, generally exhibiting physical properties that differ from its constituent pure metals.
 
• The **electrical resistivity** (ρ) of an alloy is significantly higher than that of the pure metals from which it is made, which directly increases the **electrical resistance** (R = ρl/A) of the component.
 
• According to **Joule's Law of Heating** (H = I²Rt), a higher resistance leads to the generation of more thermal energy when an electric current passes through the material.
 
• Alloys such as **Nichrome** (a blend of **nickel**, **chromium**, **manganese**, and **iron**) do not readily undergo **oxidation** or burn at high temperatures, even when they become red-hot.
 
• These properties make alloys the preferred choice for constructing **heating elements** in household appliances such as **electric irons**, **toasters**, and **room heaters**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Filaments of electric bulbs**:

 
 
• Primarily made of **Tungsten** because of its exceptionally high **melting point** (3422°C), allowing it to emit light without melting.
 
 
 
• **Connecting wires**:
 
 
• Materials like **Copper** (Cu) and **Aluminum** (Al) are used because they have extremely **low resistivity**, ensuring minimal energy loss as heat during power transmission.
 
 
 
• **Circuit fuses**:
 
 
• These use alloys of **Lead** (Pb) and **Tin** (Sn) specifically for their **low melting point**, designed to melt and break the circuit during an **overcurrent** or **short circuit**.

questions.question: Which of the following factor helps in increasing crop yield?

options.text: Using quality seeds, irrigation, fertilisers, crop protection

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Using quality seeds, irrigation, fertilisers, crop protection**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Quality seeds**, particularly **High Yielding Varieties (HYV)**, are developed to have a higher **germination rate** and better **genetic potential**, which directly correlates to a significant increase in the total biomass and grain weight produced per hectare.
 
• **Irrigation** provides a controlled and consistent water supply to the soil, which is essential for the process of **transpiration** and nutrient uptake; it mitigates the risks associated with **erratic rainfall** and **drought conditions**.
 
• **Fertilisers** supplement the soil with vital macronutrients such as **Nitrogen (N)**, **Phosphorus (P)**, and **Potassium (K)**, which are often depleted during intensive farming, ensuring optimal plant growth and metabolic functions.
 
• **Crop protection** involves the strategic use of **pesticides**, **herbicides**, and **fungicides** to shield crops from **biotic stresses** like insects, weeds, and pathogens that can otherwise destroy up to 30−40% of the potential yield.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Green Revolution**:

 
 
• Initiated in India during the **mid-1960s**, this movement focused on the **modern agricultural package** of HYV seeds, chemical inputs, and improved **irrigation infrastructure**.
 
• **M.S. Swaminathan** is widely recognized as the **Father of the Green Revolution in India** for his role in introducing high-yielding wheat and rice varieties.
 
• The use of **chemical fertilisers** helped India transition from a **ship-to-mouth** economy to a self-sufficient, food-surplus nation.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Neglecting Factors**:
 
 
• **Rainfed agriculture** is highly susceptible to **climate change**, making it less reliable for high-density food production compared to **irrigated farming**.
 
• **Poor seed quality** results in uneven plant stands and low resistance to **environmental stressors**, drastically reducing the efficiency of other inputs like water and fertilisers.

questions.question: What is the primary reason curved ceilings are used in concert halls?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To reflect sound evenly**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The use of **curved ceilings** in **concert halls** and **auditoriums** is based on the principle of the **reflection of sound**. Sound waves behave similarly to light waves when they encounter a surface.
 
• A **curved surface** (specifically **concave**) acts as a reflector that directs sound waves downward. This ensures that the sound is **evenly distributed** across the entire seating area, including the corners and the far back of the hall.
 
• When sound waves from the stage hit the **concave ceiling**, they are reflected back at specific angles (where the **angle of incidence** equals the **angle of reflection**) toward the audience.
 
• This architectural design prevents the sound from being lost in the upper reaches of the building and eliminates **acoustic shadows**, which are dead zones where sound is faint or inaudible.
 
• By creating **multiple reflections** that are directed toward the listeners, the **sound intensity** and **clarity** are significantly enhanced for everyone in the venue.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Soundboards:**

 
 
• A **soundboard** is a **curved wooden or metal board** placed behind the speaker or performer. The source of sound is placed at the **principal focus** of the board, which reflects the sound as a **parallel beam** toward the audience.
 
 
 
• **Reverberation Control:**
 
 
• While **reflection** is necessary, excessive reflection can cause **reverberation**, where sound persists too long and becomes blurred. Architects use **sound-absorbent materials** like **compressed fiberboard**, **plaster**, or **heavy draperies** to balance reflection and absorption.
 
 
 
• **Acoustic Design Elements:**
 
 
• In addition to **curved ceilings**, modern halls use **diffusers** to scatter sound randomly and **bass traps** to manage low-frequency energy, ensuring **high-fidelity audio** reproduction.

questions.question:
Select the correct option regarding the given statements.

Statement 1: Suspensions scatter light.

Statement 2: When particles settle down, they no longer scatter light.

options.text: Statement 1 is true and Statement 2 is false.
Both statements are true, and Statement 2 explains Statement 1.
Both statements are true, but Statement 2 does not explain Statement 1.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both statements are true, but Statement 2 does not explain Statement 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **suspension** is a **heterogeneous mixture** in which the solute particles do not dissolve but remain suspended throughout the bulk of the medium. These particles are large enough (typically greater than **1000 nm**) to be seen by the **naked eye** and are capable of scattering a beam of light passing through them, which makes the **path of light visible**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The scattering of light by particles in a mixture is known as the **Tyndall Effect**. In a suspension, this effect is prominent as long as the particles remain distributed in the **solvent**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• Suspensions are inherently **unstable** systems. When left undisturbed for a period, the relatively large and heavy particles settle down at the bottom of the container due to the force of **gravity**, a process known as **sedimentation**. Once the particles have settled, the mixture loses its **turbidity** and its ability to scatter light effectively because the large particles are no longer in the path of the beam. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• While both statements are scientifically accurate, the fact that particles stop scattering light after settling (Statement 2) is a result of the mixture's **instability** and does not provide the causal mechanism for why suspensions scatter light in their active state (Statement 1). The scattering is fundamentally caused by **particle size** and **optical interference**. ***Hence, statement 2 does not explain statement 1.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Mixtures based on Particle Size**:

 
 
• **True Solutions**: These are **homogeneous mixtures** with a particle size less than **1 nm**. They do not scatter light, and the path of the beam is not visible.
 
• **Colloids**: These mixtures have particle sizes between **1 nm and 1000 nm**. They are stable and do not settle, yet they are large enough to exhibit the **Tyndall Effect**.
 
• **Suspensions**: These have the largest particles (over **1000 nm**). They scatter light but are **unstable** and can be separated by **filtration**.
 
 
 
• **Physical Separation**:
 
 
• Unlike solutions and colloids, the particles of a **suspension** can be separated from the mixture using **filter paper** because of their large dimensions.

questions.question: The urine formed in the kidneys passes through the ______ into the _____ where it is stored until excreted.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ureters; urinary bladder**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Urinary System** consists of the kidneys, ureters, urinary bladder, and urethra, working together to filter blood and eliminate liquid waste.
 
• Urine is continuously produced in the **Kidneys** through the filtration of blood and then travels to the **Renal Pelvis**, a funnel-shaped structure.
 
• The **Ureters** are two muscular tubes, typically **25 to 30 cm** (10-12 inches) long, that connect each kidney to the urinary bladder.
 
• Urine does not flow simply by gravity; the **Smooth Muscles** in the walls of the ureters create waves of **Peristalsis** to force urine downward into the bladder.
 
• The **Urinary Bladder** is a hollow, distensible muscular organ located in the **Pelvic Cavity** that serves as a reservoir for storing urine until it is excreted.
 
• In a healthy adult, the bladder can hold approximately **400 to 600 mL** of urine before the pressure triggers the urge to urinate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Urethra**:

 
 
• This is the final canal through which urine is discharged from the body during **Micturition**.
 
• In biological females, the urethra is short (about **4 cm**), while in biological males, it is longer (about **20 cm**) and also serves as a passage for semen.
 
 
 
• **Nephrons**:
 
 
• These are the microscopic structural and functional units of the kidney, with each kidney containing approximately **1 million** nephrons.
 
• They perform three primary processes: **Glomerular Filtration**, **Tubular Reabsorption**, and **Tubular Secretion** to maintain blood **Homeostasis**.
 
 
 
• **Internal and External Sphincters**:
 
 
• The **Internal Urethral Sphincter** is involuntary, whereas the **External Urethral Sphincter** is under voluntary control, allowing humans to decide when to release urine.

questions.question:
Read the following statements carefully and choose the correct option.

Statement 1: Members of a homologous series differ by a –CH₂– group.

Statement 2: Each successive member of a homologous series differs from the previous one by 12 u in molecular mass.

options.text: Both statements are true and Statement 2 is the correct explanation of Statement 1.
Statement 1 is true but Statement 2 is false.
Both statements are true but Statement 2 is not the correct explanation of Statement 1.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Statement 1 is true but Statement 2 is false**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **homologous series** is defined as a sequence of **organic compounds** that possess the same **functional group** and similar chemical properties, where each successive member differs from the previous one by a **methylene unit**, which is the **-CH2-** group. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The **molecular mass** of any member in a series is determined by the sum of the atomic masses of its constituent atoms. Since successive members differ by a **-CH2-** group, the difference in their molecular masses is calculated as the mass of one **Carbon** atom (**12 u**) plus two **Hydrogen** atoms (**2 × 1 u**), totaling **14 u**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Characteristics of Homologous Series:**

 
 
• **General Formula:** All members of a specific series can be represented by a single **general molecular formula**. For instance, **Alkanes** follow **CₙH₂ₙ₊₂**, **Alkenes** follow **CₙH₂ₙ**, and **Alkynes** follow **CₙH₂ₙ−₂**.
 
• **Chemical Properties:** Because they share the same **functional group**, all members exhibit almost identical **chemical reactions**.
 
• **Physical Properties:** There is a gradual **gradation** in physical properties such as **melting point**, **boiling point**, and **solubility** as the **molecular mass** increases. For example, the boiling point increases with the increase in the number of carbon atoms due to stronger **Van der Waals forces**.
 
• **Example Calculation:** In the **Alkane** series, **Methane** (CH₄) has a mass of **16 u**, while **Ethane** (C₂H₆) has a mass of **30 u**. The difference is **30 − 16 = 14 u**, which corresponds to the **-CH2-** unit.

questions.question: The symbol ‘B’ represents which element?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Boron**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The chemical symbol **B** represents **Boron**, which is a chemical element with the **atomic number 5**.
 
• It is classified as a **metalloid**, meaning it exhibits properties intermediate between those of typical metals and non-metals.
 
• Boron is located in **Group 13** and **Period 2** of the **Periodic Table**, serving as the head of the boron group.
 
• The **electronic configuration** of Boron is **1s² 2s² 2p¹**, indicating it has three electrons in its outermost shell.
 
• It is a rare element in the **Solar System** and Earth's crust, primarily produced by **cosmic ray spallation** and not by stellar nucleosynthesis.
 
• Boron is never found as a free element on Earth; it occurs naturally in water-soluble compounds such as **borates**, **borax**, and **boric acid**.
 
• The element was first isolated in **1808** by the French chemists **Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac** and **Louis Jacques Thénard**, and independently by the British chemist **Sir Humphry Davy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Beryllium (Be)**:

 
 
• Identified by the symbol **Be** with **atomic number 4**.
 
• It is a steel-gray, strong, and lightweight **alkaline earth metal** used in high-speed aircraft and satellite components.
 
 
 
• **Barium (Ba)**:
 
 
• Represented by the symbol **Ba** with **atomic number 56**.
 
• A soft, silvery-white metal belonging to the **alkaline earth metal** group, frequently used in **drilling fluids** for oil wells and as a contrast agent in **medical imaging**.
 
 
 
• **Bromine (Br)**:
 
 
• Represented by the symbol **Br** with **atomic number 35**.
 
• It is a member of the **Halogen** group and is the only non-metallic element that is a **liquid** at room temperature.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Boron**:
 
 
• Boron is essential for the cell walls of **plants** and is used in the manufacture of **borosilicate glass**, which is highly resistant to thermal shock.
 
• In **nuclear technology**, Boron-10 is used as a **neutron absorber** in the control rods of nuclear reactors due to its high neutron capture cross-section.

questions.question: When potassium reacts with water, we observe:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bright flame and rapid reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Potassium (K)** is an **Alkali Metal** located in **Group 1** of the periodic table, characterized by its extreme chemical reactivity due to a single valence electron.
 
• When potassium comes into contact with water, a highly **exothermic reaction** occurs, represented by the chemical equation: 2K + 2H₂O → 2KOH + H₂.
 
• The reaction produces **Potassium Hydroxide** and releases **Hydrogen gas**. The heat generated is so intense that it causes the evolved hydrogen gas to ignite almost instantly.
 
• This combustion results in a distinctive **lilac-colored flame** (light purple), which is a signature identification for the presence of potassium ions.
 
• During the process, the metal reacts so **rapidly** that it melts into a small silvery ball and skims across the surface of the water before eventually disappearing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reactivity of Group 1 Metals**:

 
 
• **Lithium**: Reacts slowly with water, causing steady **effervescence** (bubbling) as hydrogen is released, but it does not usually catch fire.
 
• **Sodium**: Reacts vigorously and melts into a ball, producing a **yellow flame** if the hydrogen ignites.
 
• **Rubidium and Caesium**: These are even more reactive than potassium and react **explosively** even with cold water.
 
 
 
• **Storage Protocols**: Because potassium reacts violently with **atmospheric moisture** and oxygen, it must be stored submerged in **kerosene** or **paraffin oil** to maintain its metallic state.
 
• **Density**: Potassium is **less dense than water**, which is why it floats and moves on the surface during the chemical reaction.

questions.question: Dhritiman tries to extract magnesium from magnesium oxide using carbon. The attempt fails. What is the reason?

options.text: The reaction produces carbon monoxide only.
Magnesium forms a volatile compound with carbon.
Carbon is less reactive than magnesium.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon is less reactive than magnesium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Magnesium** is placed **above carbon** in the **reactivity series**, making it **more reactive** than carbon.
 
• Carbon can reduce the oxides of metals that are **less reactive than carbon**, such as **zinc, iron, and lead**, but it **cannot reduce magnesium oxide (MgO)**.
 
• **Magnesium oxide (MgO)** is a highly stable compound with a strong ionic bond, requiring **electrolysis** rather than carbon reduction for the extraction of magnesium.
 
• Industrial extraction of **magnesium** is carried out by the **electrolysis of molten magnesium chloride (MgCl₂)**, not by heating magnesium oxide with carbon.
 
• ***Hence, the attempt fails because carbon is less reactive than magnesium.***

• **Potassium, Sodium, Calcium, Magnesium, Aluminium, Carbon, Zinc, Iron, Lead, Copper, Silver, Gold** (decreasing order of reactivity).
 
• Metals above carbon in the series cannot be extracted by carbon reduction.
 
 
 
• **Carbon Reduction:**
 
 
• Carbon acts as a **reducing agent** by removing oxygen from metal oxides.
 
• It is effective only for metals that are **less reactive than carbon**.
 
 
 
• **Extraction of Magnesium:**
 
 
• Commercially obtained by the **electrolysis of molten magnesium chloride**.
 
• This process produces **magnesium at the cathode** and **chlorine gas at the anode**.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Metals Extracted by Carbon Reduction:**
 
 
• **Iron** from **hematite (Fe₂O₃)**.
 
• **Zinc** from **zinc oxide (ZnO)**.
 
• **Lead** from **lead oxide (PbO)**.
 
 
 
• **Highly Reactive Metals:**
 
 
• **Potassium, Sodium, Calcium, Magnesium, and Aluminium** are generally extracted by **electrolysis** because chemical reducing agents like carbon cannot displace them from their compounds.

• **Statement 2**: This model assumed mass was distributed uniformly; however, the **nucleus** and **neutrons** were not yet discovered. The **nucleus** was identified by **Ernest Rutherford** in **1911**, and **neutrons** by **James Chadwick** in **1932**. Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.

__
 
• **Simple columnar epithelium** consists of a single layer of tall, slender cells with nuclei usually located near the **basal surface**.
 
• This tissue is primarily found lining the **digestive tract**, specifically the **stomach**, **small intestine**, and **large intestine**, where it performs critical functions of **secretion** and **absorption**.
 
• In the **human intestine**, these cells are specialized with **microvilli** on their apical surface, which significantly increases the **surface area** available for the absorption of nutrients and water.

• **Stratified squamous epithelium**:

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the universal law of gravitation?

options.text: The gravitational force decreases when the masses of the objects increase.
The gravitational force depends only on the distance between the objects, not their masses.
The gravitational force increases as the distance between objects increases.
The gravitational force increases with the product of the masses and decreases with the square of the distance between them.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The gravitational force increases with the product of the masses and decreases with the square of the distance between them.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Universal Law of Gravitation**, formulated by **Sir Isaac Newton** in 1687, describes the attractive force between any two objects with mass in the universe.
 
• According to this law, the **magnitude of the force** (F) is **directly proportional** to the product of the masses of the two interacting objects ( m₁ times m₂ ). **Hence, statement 4 is partially correct regarding mass proportionality.**
 
• The law further specifies that the force is **inversely proportional** to the **square of the distance** ( r² ) between the centers of the two objects. This is known as the **inverse-square law**. **Hence, statement 4 is fully correct.**
 
• Mathematically, the relationship is expressed as F = G (m₁ m₂)/(r²) , where **G** represents the **Universal Gravitational Constant**.
 
• The force acts along the **line joining the centers** of the two masses, making it a **central force** that is always **attractive** in nature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Universal Gravitational Constant (G)**:

 
 
• The value of **G** is constant throughout the universe and is approximately 6.674 times 10⁻¹¹ { N m}² { kg}⁻² .
 
• This constant was first accurately measured by **Henry Cavendish** in 1798 using a **torsion balance**.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Gravitational Force**:
 
 
• It is the **weakest** of the four fundamental forces of nature but has an **infinite range**.
 
• It does not depend on the **medium** between the two objects.
 
• It obeys **Newtons Third Law of Motion**, as the forces exerted by the two bodies on each other are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.
 
• It is a **conservative force**, meaning the work done by gravity depends only on the initial and final positions, not the path taken.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are true regarding the magnetic field line pattern around a straight current carrying wire?

(i) The magnetic field lines around a current carrying wire are in the form of concentric circles.

(ii) The magnetic field lines around a current carrying wire intersect at various points.

(iii) The magnetic field lines move farther apart as one moves away from the wire.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (i) and (iii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The magnetic field lines around a **straight current-carrying conductor** are in the form of **concentric circles** that are centered on the wire and exist in a plane perpendicular to the wire. **Hence, statement (i) is correct.**
 
• Magnetic field lines **never intersect** each other because if they did, it would mean that at the point of intersection, a magnetic compass would point in **two different directions** simultaneously, which is physically impossible. **Hence, statement (ii) is incorrect.**
 
• The **magnitude** of the magnetic field produced by a straight wire decreases as the distance from the wire increases. To represent this weakening **field intensity** graphically, the circular field lines are drawn **farther apart** as the distance from the conductor increases. **Hence, statement (iii) is correct.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Right-Hand Thumb Rule**:

 
 
• This rule is used to determine the **direction** of magnetic field lines.
 
• If the thumb of the right hand points in the direction of the **electric current**, the curled fingers indicate the direction of the **magnetic field**.
 
 
 
• **Mathematical Relation**:
 
 
• The magnetic field strength **B** is directly proportional to the **current (I)** passing through the wire.
 
• The magnetic field strength **B** is inversely proportional to the **distance (r)** from the wire, represented by the relationship **B ∝ I / r**.
 
 
 
• **Oersted's Discovery**:
 
 
• **Hans Christian Oersted** first observed in **1820** that a compass needle is deflected when placed near a wire carrying an electric current, proving that electricity and **magnetism** are related.

questions.question: For an object moving with uniform velocity, the height of its velocity-time graph remains constant with time. This results in a graph that is a _________.

options.text: Straight line passing through the origin
Straight line parallel to the x-axis

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Straight line parallel to the x-axis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uniform velocity** occurs when an object covers equal **displacements** in equal intervals of time, implying that both **speed** and **direction** remain constant throughout the motion.
 
• In a **velocity-time (v-t) graph**, time is conventionally plotted on the **horizontal x-axis**, while velocity is plotted on the **vertical y-axis**.
 
• Because the velocity does not change with respect to time, the **y-coordinate** (representing velocity) remains fixed at a specific value for every point on the **time axis**.
 
• Geometrically, a set of points sharing the same **ordinal value** (constant height) results in a **horizontal straight line** that never intersects the x-axis unless the velocity is zero.
 
• The **slope** of a velocity-time graph represents the **acceleration** of the object; for uniform velocity, the change in velocity is zero, resulting in a **zero slope**, which corresponds to a line **parallel to the x-axis**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Displacement from Graph**:

 
 
• The **area under the curve** in a velocity-time graph provides the **total displacement** of the object. For uniform motion, this area is a **rectangle** with the formula **Displacement = Velocity × Time**.
 
 
 
• **Straight line passing through the origin**:
 
 
• This specific graph shape represents **uniform acceleration** where the object starts from a **state of rest** (initial velocity is zero). The velocity increases linearly with time.
 
 
 
• **Curve**:
 
 
• A **non-linear** or curved line on a v-t graph indicates **variable acceleration**, where the rate of change of velocity is not constant over time.
 
 
 
• **Vertical line**:
 
 
• A line parallel to the y-axis is **physically impossible** in kinematics as it would suggest an object possesses multiple velocities at the exact same instant or has **infinite acceleration**.

questions.question: Which quantity decreases when a solid object is immersed in water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Apparent weight**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a solid object is immersed in water, it experiences an upward force known as the **buoyant force** or **upthrust**. This phenomenon is governed by **Archimedes’ Principle**, which states that the upward buoyant force is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by the object.
 
• The **apparent weight** is the net downward force acting on the object while it is submerged. It is calculated by the formula: **Apparent Weight = True Weight − Buoyant Force**.
 
• Because the **buoyant force** acts in the opposite direction to the **force of gravity** (true weight), the effective weight of the object decreases, making it feel lighter than its actual weight in a vacuum or air.
 
• The magnitude of this decrease depends directly on the **density of the fluid** and the **volume of the displaced fluid**. In water, which has a high density compared to air, this reduction is significant and easily measurable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mass**:

 
 
• It is an **intrinsic property** of matter representing the quantity of atoms and molecules in an object.
 
• Mass is a **scalar quantity** and remains constant regardless of the object's location or the medium it is placed in.
 
 
 
• **Density**:
 
 
• Defined as the **mass per unit volume** of a substance. For a solid, non-porous object, neither its total mass nor its physical volume changes upon immersion.
 
• Therefore, the **density** remains **invariant** during the process of immersion in water.
 
 
 
• **Buoyant Force**:
 
 
• This force is an **interaction** between the fluid and the object. It does not decrease; rather, it is the **exerted pressure** from the fluid that creates the upward lift.
 
• It is calculated as **ρ × g × V**, where ρ is the density of the fluid, g is **acceleration due to gravity**, and V is the submerged volume.
