questions.question: If the force of gravitation between the Earth and the Moon is ' F ' N, then how much will be the force between the Earth and the Moon if the distance between them is doubled? (Keep all the other parameters the same.)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**F/4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation** states that the force of attraction between two objects is directly proportional to the product of their masses and **inversely proportional to the square of the distance** between their centers.
 
• The mathematical formula for this force is **F = G (m₁ × m₂) / r²**, where **F** represents the gravitational force, **G** is the universal gravitational constant, **m₁** and **m₂** are the masses of the two bodies, and **r** is the distance between them.
 
• Initially, the force between the **Earth** and the **Moon** is given as **F**. If the initial distance is **r**, then **F = G (Mₑ × Mₘ) / r²**.
 
• According to the problem, the distance is doubled, meaning the new distance **r'** is equal to **2r**. All other parameters, including the **masses** and the **gravitational constant**, remain unchanged.
 
• Substituting the new distance into the formula, the new force **F'** becomes **G (Mₑ × Mₘ) / (2r)²**, which simplifies to **G (Mₑ × Mₘ) / 4r²**.
 
• Comparing the two equations, **F' = (1/4) × [G (Mₑ × Mₘ) / r²]**, which simplifies to **F' = F/4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inverse Square Law**:

 
 
• This law is a fundamental principle in physics where a specified physical quantity or intensity is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the source.
 
• In the context of gravity, if the distance is **tripled**, the force becomes **F/9**; if the distance is **halved**, the force increases to **4F**.
 
 
 
• **Universal Gravitational Constant (G)**:
 
 
• The value of **G** is approximately **6.674 × 10−¹¹ N m² kg−²**.
 
• It was first measured by **Henry Cavendish** in 1798.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Gravitational Force**:
 
 
• It is the **weakest** of the four fundamental forces in nature but has an **infinite range**.
 
• It is a **central force**, acting along the line joining the centers of the two interacting masses.
 
• It is **independent** of the medium between the two bodies.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the cell wall in plant cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Provide rigidity and protection**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **cell wall** is a non-living, rigid, and semi-permeable outer layer found in plant cells, situated outside the **cell membrane**.
 
• Its primary chemical component in plants is **cellulose**, a complex polysaccharide that provides high **tensile strength** and structural durability.
 
• The main function is to provide **structural support** and **rigidity**, allowing plants to grow to significant heights and maintain a defined shape without an internal skeleton.
 
• It serves as a **protective barrier** that shields the cell from mechanical stress, physical injury, and infection by pathogens like bacteria or fungi.
 
• The cell wall helps the cell withstand **turgor pressure**; this internal pressure exerted by the central vacuole keeps the plant **turgid** and prevents the cell from bursting in **hypotonic** environments.
 
• It facilitates communication and transport between adjacent cells through **plasmodesmata**, which are narrow channels crossing the cell walls.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cell Wall Composition**:

 
 
• In **fungi**, the cell wall is primarily made of **chitin**, which is also found in the exoskeletons of arthropods.
 
• In **bacteria**, the wall is composed of **peptidoglycan** (murein), which is essential for survival in diverse osmotic conditions.
 
• **Algal** cell walls often contain cellulose along with other substances like **galactans**, **mannans**, and **calcium carbonate**.
 
 
 
• **Cellular Respiration**: This process is managed by the **mitochondria**, often called the **powerhouse of the cell**, where glucose is oxidized to produce **ATP**.
 
• **Cell Division**: This is a complex process regulated by the **nucleus**, which contains the **genetic material** (DNA), and involves structures like **spindle fibers**.
 
• **Nutrient Transport**: While the cell wall allows the passage of water and solutes, the **plasma membrane** is the structure responsible for **selective permeability**, controlling exactly which substances enter or leave the cell.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for the establishment of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) to safeguard the rights of the Scheduled Castes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 338**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 338** of the **Constitution of India** mandates the establishment of the **National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC)**, a **constitutional body** dedicated to protecting the rights of the **Scheduled Castes**.
 
• The commission is entrusted with the duty to investigate and monitor all matters relating to the safeguards provided for the **Scheduled Castes** under the **Constitution** or any other laws of the country.
 
• The **89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003**, bifurcated the former joint commission into two separate entities: the **National Commission for Scheduled Castes** under **Article 338** and the **National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST)** under **Article 338A**.
 
• The **NCSC** consists of a **Chairperson**, a **Vice-Chairperson**, and **three other members**, all of whom are appointed by the **President of India** by warrant under his hand and seal.
 
• While investigating any matter or inquiry, the commission possesses all the powers of a **Civil Court**, specifically regarding the summoning of witnesses and the production of documents.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 340**:

 
 
• Empowers the **President** to appoint a commission to investigate the conditions of socially and educationally **backward classes**.
 
• This article formed the basis for the establishment of the **Mandal Commission** in **1979**.
 
 
 
• **Article 330**:
 
 
• Provides for the **reservation of seats** for the **Scheduled Castes** and the **Scheduled Tribes** in the **House of the People** (Lok Sabha).
 
• The number of reserved seats is determined by the proportion of their population in each **State** or **Union Territory**.
 
 
 
• **Article 350**:
 
 
• Relates to the language to be used in representations for the **redress of grievances** to any authority of the **Union** or a **State**.
 
• It is associated with **Article 350B**, which provides for a **Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities**.

questions.question: Who was chosen as the first president of the Indian National Congress (INC) during its first session?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian National Congress** (INC) held its inaugural session from **December 28 to December 31, 1885**, marking the beginning of a structured national movement in India.
 
• **Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee**, a distinguished **Bengali barrister**, was elected as the **first President** of the session, representing the **Moderate** phase of Indian politics.
 
• The venue for this historic meeting was **Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College** in **Bombay** (present-day Mumbai).

questions.question: Which of the following British Indian government legislations provided for the establishment of a Supreme Court at Calcutta, comprising one chief justice and three other judges?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Regulating Act of 1773**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Regulating Act of 1773** was the first major step taken by the **British Parliament** to exercise control over the **East India Company’s** administration in **India**.
 
• Section 13 of this legislation specifically authorized the **British Crown** to establish a **Supreme Court of Judicature** at **Fort William** in **Calcutta**.
 
• The Act mandated that the court would consist of a **Chief Justice** and **three other judges** (Puisne Judges) to oversee legal matters involving **British subjects** and those in the service of the Company.
 
• Established in **1774**, the court functioned as a **Court of Record** with wide-ranging civil and criminal jurisdiction; **Sir Elijah Impey** was appointed as the first **Chief Justice**.
 
• The Act also transformed the **Governor of Bengal** into the **Governor-General of Bengal**, with **Warren Hastings** being the first to hold this prestigious post.
 
• It prohibited the employees of the **East India Company** from engaging in any **private trade** or accepting **presents and bribes** from the local population to curb corruption.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pitt’s India Act of 1784**:

 
 
• This Act introduced a **system of double government** by establishing the **Board of Control** to supervise political and military affairs.
 
• It clearly distinguished between the **commercial** and **political functions** of the Company for the first time.
 
 
 
• **Amending Act of 1781**:
 
 
• Known as the **Act of Settlement**, it was passed to rectify the defects and jurisdictional ambiguities of the **Regulating Act of 1773**.
 
• It exempted the **Governor-General and Council** from the jurisdiction of the **Supreme Court** for their official acts.
 
 
 
• **Charter Act of 1793**:
 
 
• It renewed the **East India Company’s monopoly** over **Indian trade** for an additional period of **twenty years**.
 
• It laid down the rule that the members of the **Board of Control** would be paid out of **Indian revenues**.

__
 
• The **Ministry of Home Affairs** (MHA) has proposed to amend **Article 240** of the **Constitution of India** to include the **Union Territory** of **Chandigarh** within its ambit.
 
• **Article 240** empowers the **President of India** to make regulations for the peace, progress, and good government of certain **Union Territories**, which have the same force as an **Act of Parliament**.
 
• Currently, **Chandigarh** does not have its own legislative assembly, and most laws are extended from the state of **Punjab** or enacted directly by the **Parliament**.
 
• The proposed inclusion aims to streamline the legislative process, allowing the **President** to enact specific regulations for **Chandigarh** without requiring a formal **Parliamentary** session for every administrative requirement.
 
• This move is intended to enhance **ease of doing business** and simplify the legal framework governing the city's unique administrative structure as a joint capital.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 240**:

 
 
• Specifically covers **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**, **Lakshadweep**, **Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu**, and **Puducherry**.
 
• For **Puducherry**, the **President** can only make regulations when the **Legislative Assembly** is dissolved or suspended.
 
 
 
• **New Delhi**:
 
 
• Governed under **Article 239AA**, which provides a special status with a **Legislative Assembly** and a **Council of Ministers**.
 
• It is not included under **Article 240** because it has its own dedicated constitutional framework for governance.
 
 
 
• **Chandigarh Administration**:
 
 
• It was constituted as a **Union Territory** on **November 1, 1966**, following the reorganization of **Punjab**.
 
• It is managed by an **Administrator** appointed under **Article 239**, traditionally the **Governor of Punjab**.
